topic: Atomic Structure: Subatomic Particles, Electronic Configuration & Isotopes (Set 2)

questions.question: How many protons, neutrons, and electrons are present in an ion of aluminium with a +3 charge? (Aluminium atomic number = 13, mass number = 27)
questions.explanation: Protons = 13. Neutrons = 27 - 13 = 14. Electrons = 13 - 3 (due to the +3 charge) = 10.

questions.question: How many protons, neutrons, and electrons are present in an ion of oxygen with a -2 charge? (Oxygen atomic number = 8, mass number = 16)
questions.explanation: Protons = 8. Neutrons = 16 - 8 = 8. Electrons = 8 + 2 (due to the -2 charge) = 10.

questions.question: A sample of chlorine contains 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is the relative atomic mass of chlorine?
Element X consists of two isotopes: 60% abundance of the isotope with mass number 69, and 40% abundance of the isotope with mass number 71. What is the relative atomic mass of X?
An element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 8, 1. In which Period and Group is it located?
questions.explanation: Four occupied shells means Period 4. One valence electron means Group 1. (This is Potassium).

questions.question: Element P is in Group 2 and Element Q is in Group 7. What is the combining ratio of atoms in the compound formed between them?
options: One P atom for every one Q atom
One P atom for every two Q atoms
Two P atoms for every one Q atom
Two P atoms for every seven Q atoms
questions.explanation: Group 2 elements form ions with a +2 charge. Group 7 elements form ions with a -1 charge. To balance the charges, two Q ions are needed for every P ion.

questions.question: When a neutral atom loses two electrons to form an ion, what happens to its nucleon number?
questions.explanation: The nucleon number is the sum of protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Losing electrons does not change the composition of the nucleus.

questions.question: What is the definition of relative atomic mass?
options: The mass of one atom of an element in grams
The average mass of an atom of an element compared to one-twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom
The sum of protons and electrons in an atom
The mass of one mole of a substance
questions.explanation: Relative atomic mass is the weighted average mass of an atom of an element relative to one-twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a negligible relative mass?
questions.explanation: The electron has a relative mass of approximately 1/1840, which is considered negligible in mass number calculations.

questions.question: When a beam of protons, neutrons, and electrons passes through an electric field, which particle is deflected the most?
questions.explanation: The electron is deflected the most because it has the highest charge-to-mass ratio, despite having the same magnitude of charge as a proton.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs represents isotopes of the same element?
questions.explanation: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 both have 6 protons (making them Carbon) but different numbers of neutrons (6 and 8, respectively), making them isotopes.

questions.question: What is the electronic configuration of a magnesium ion with a +2 charge?
questions.explanation: Neutral magnesium is 2, 8, 2. Losing two valence electrons to form a +2 ion leaves the configuration as 2, 8.

questions.question: What is the electronic configuration of a sulfide ion with a -2 charge? (Neutral sulfur is 2, 8, 6)
questions.explanation: Neutral sulfur gains two electrons to achieve a full outer shell, changing its configuration from 2, 8, 6 to 2, 8, 8.

questions.question: How many total electrons are present in a hydroxide ion with a -1 charge? (Oxygen has 8 protons, Hydrogen has 1 proton)
questions.explanation: Oxygen contributes 8 electrons, Hydrogen contributes 1 electron, and the -1 charge indicates 1 extra electron. Total = 8 + 1 + 1 = 10.

questions.question: An atom has 3 valence electrons and 3 occupied electron shells. Which element is it?
questions.explanation: 3 occupied shells means Period 3. 3 valence electrons means Group 3 (or 13). The configuration is 2, 8, 3, which is Aluminium (atomic number 13).

questions.question: An element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 18, 8, 2. Which group does it belong to?
questions.explanation: The number of outer shell (valence) electrons determines the group for main group elements. With 2 valence electrons, it is in Group 2.

questions.question: What is the charge of the nucleus of an oxygen atom?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains 8 protons, each with a +1 charge, and 8 neutrons with 0 charge. The overall nuclear charge is +8.

questions.question: How many occupied electron shells are there in a neutral atom of potassium (atomic number 19)?
questions.explanation: The electronic configuration of potassium is 2, 8, 8, 1. This occupies 4 electron shells, placing it in Period 4.

questions.question: Why do metal atoms typically form positive ions?
options: They gain protons to become stable
They lose valence electrons to achieve a full outer shell
They gain neutrons to increase their mass
They share electrons equally with other metals
questions.explanation: Metals have 1, 2, or 3 valence electrons. It is energetically favorable for them to lose these electrons to achieve a stable, full outer shell, forming a positive ion.

questions.question: Why do non-metal atoms typically form negative ions?
options: They lose protons to become stable
They gain electrons to achieve a full outer shell
They lose neutrons to decrease their mass
questions.explanation: Non-metals have 5, 6, or 7 valence electrons. It is energetically favorable for them to gain electrons to achieve a stable, full outer shell, forming a negative ion.

questions.question: What is the relative mass of a proton?
questions.explanation: Both protons and neutrons are assigned a relative mass of 1 for simplicity in chemical calculations.

questions.question: An atom has 15 protons and 16 neutrons. What is its nucleon number?
questions.explanation: Nucleon number = protons + neutrons = 15 + 16 = 31.

questions.question: Which statement about the nucleus of an atom is correct?
options: It is very large compared to the total volume of the atom
It contains protons and neutrons and has a positive charge
It has a negative charge due to the presence of electrons
questions.explanation: The nucleus is very small and dense, contains protons and neutrons, and carries an overall positive charge.

questions.question: Two atoms, X and Y, have the same atomic number but different mass numbers. What can be concluded?
options: They are isotopes of the same element
They have different numbers of electrons in their neutral state
questions.explanation: Same atomic number means they are the same element. Different mass numbers mean they have different numbers of neutrons, which is the definition of isotopes.
